teaser: A reply to Bert Kok: agents that augment journalists, publishers that own the now cheap stack, and the reader's trust above all.
core_idea: Bert Kok is right that AI platforms now own synthesis and the interface while publishers fund costly discovery; the knowledge architecture and reader feedback loop the essay calls for already exist in our open-source stack, where agents augment rather than replace journalists, so publishers should own that cheap stack and, above all, the reader's trust.

figures.caption: What we have built, in twelve pages: this newsroom's front page; the PHP October 2026 story site; its state of affairs, versioned; its source watch of 913 pages; Wikipedia's article on the flaw, read as a graph; the control room for its 23 agents; the bridge, a local story kept as a graph; the waiting room that knew first; a desk kept in a vault; the Industry Wire; the World News Day corpus; and Pulse, exploited against talked about.
Bert Kok's post on LinkedIn, 25 October 2026, sharing the essay for The News Stack: "Publishers may fund the most expensive layer and capture the least valuable".

My reply under Bert Kok's post, 25 October 2026: thinking along very similar lines, building MVPs that show how the data behind a story can be captured, linked and monetised, and this article to follow.
